canonical_question: Does the success of the coating on 'Mo-Re alloys' at Mach 4 imply it will perform similarly against the mechanical erosion in hypersonic flight?

question_variants.question: Does the success of the coating on 'Mo-Re alloys' at Mach 4 imply it will perform similarly against the mechanical erosion in hypersonic flight?
question_variants.resolution_summary: The provided evidence cites good oxidation protection at Mach 4 but does not contain data or statements regarding performance against mechanical erosion, which is distinct from oxidation resistance. The transfer from oxidation to erosion cannot be confirmed by the supplied text.

answers.answer: The technical report reported good oxidation protection for Mo-Re alloys at Mach 4, but the evidence does not address mechanical erosion resistance or validate performance in that specific failure mode.
answers.boundary_limitation: No data on mechanical erosion provided
evidence_spans: The aim of this paper is to explore the feasibility of the Si-20Cr-20Fe coating in improving the oxidation resistance of MoNbTaTiW RHEA. The Si-20Cr-20Fe coating was prepared on the surface of MoNbTaTiW RHEA by a fused slurry method. To show the anti-oxidation mechanism of the silicide coating, the evolution of the structure and compositions of the coating at 1000 °C and 1300 °C were studied.

source_evidence_spans: The technical report (NASA TN contractor report 201753) reported that the Si-20Cr-20Fe coating provided very good oxidation protection for Mo-Re alloys at 1260 °C and Mach 4
